question: Does training longer actually produce a better model, by enough to beat the run-to-run luck of a different random start?
why_this_is_worth_asking: The studio offers three practice lengths and tells the user longer is better.
Nothing in the repository has ever measured whether that is true on this corpus,
or by how much, or whether the difference survives changing the random seed.
A preset that promises 'better results, if you can wait' is a claim, and it has

fixed_across_every_run.split: group_split defaults (val_frac 0.1, seed 1337) - IDENTICAL holdout for every run, so arms are compared on the same text
fixed_across_every_run.architecture: Medium preset: n_layer 4, n_head 4, n_embd 256, block_size 128, batch_size 32
fixed_across_every_run.lr: auto_lr(256), the width-scaled default the GUI uses
fixed_across_every_run.eval: estimate_loss on the dedicated eval RNG (EVAL_SEED 12345), so evaluation cannot perturb training

arms.note_on_seed: The seed varies model initialisation and the training batch stream. It does NOT vary the split - Corpus takes a hardcoded split seed - which is what we want here: every arm is scored on the same held-out text.

primary_outcome: final validation loss (nats/char) on the fixed holdout
secondary_outcome: closed_fraction - how much of the distance the trigram lookup table could NOT cover the model covered. Reported because validation loss alone cannot say whether a number is good.
noise_floor_definition: For each arm, the spread (max - min) of the 5 seeds. This is how much the answer moves for reasons that have nothing to do with the thing being tested.

success_bar.primary: A step-count increase counts as a REAL improvement only if the gap between the two arms' MEANS is larger than the WIDER of the two arms' seed spreads.
success_bar.rationale: If changing the random seed moves the answer more than changing the training length does, then the training length is not what is being measured.

prespecified_outcomes.if_gaps_beat_noise: Report that longer training measurably helps on this corpus, with the measured gap and the measured noise, and the preset wording is supported.
prespecified_outcomes.if_gaps_are_inside_noise: Report that on this corpus, at these sizes, the difference between practice lengths is not distinguishable from run-to-run luck - and say so plainly rather than quietly not mentioning it.
prespecified_outcomes.either_way: Both outcomes get published. A null result here is a real finding about the preset.

not_claimed: That these numbers transfer to another corpus, another architecture, or another vocabulary.
That validation loss is a proxy for whether the generated text is any good.
That 5 seeds is enough to detect a small effect; it is enough to detect an effect larger than the spread it measures.
That the trigram baseline is the strongest possible baseline - it is deliberately weak, see baselines.py.
